method: Headlines collected via web search (fetch_news.py collector blocked in sandbox; use it for local/Actions runs). Entity sentiment scored by Claude during the weekly Cowork routine. sentiment = 0-100 D-favorability of coverage tone (matches existing dashboard sentimentScore semantics: >55 leans D, <45 leans R). candidateSentiment = 0-100 favorability of coverage toward that candidate personally. outletLean: -2 left ... +2 right (AllSides-style); null = unrated outlet, excluded from scatter.

races.matchup: Susan Collins (R, inc.) vs. Troy Jackson (D)
races.summary: Coverage over the past two weeks centered on polling that shows Democrat Troy Jackson with a narrow edge over five-term GOP Sen. Susan Collins. A Fox News poll (Aug. 6-10) had Jackson up 48-46, and a Senate Majority PAC/Hart Research survey put him ahead 49-45, with the RealClearPolitics average showing Jackson +2.3. Reporting emphasized that 55% of Maine voters worry Collins votes with Trump too often, outweighing concerns that Jackson is too progressive, though Republicans note Collins trailed by similar margins in 2020 before winning. The Senate Leadership Fund is already running attack ads tying Jackson to the left, and Graham Platner's withdrawal continued to shadow the race.

articles.headline: Where things stand in the Susan Collins-Troy Jackson Maine Senate race
Susan Collins poll finds Trump's ties worry Maine voters more than DSA
Maine voters say Susan Collins votes with Trump too often in Fox News poll

races.matchup: Hannah Pingree (D) vs. Bobby Charles (R) vs. Rick Bennett (I)
races.summary: Coverage in early August continued to portray Democrat Hannah Pingree as the clear front-runner to succeed term-limited Gov. Janet Mills. Pingree picked up the Maine Education Association (teachers union) endorsement on Aug. 6, adding to earlier backing from Planned Parenthood's action fund and a large fundraising advantage over both rivals. Republican Bobby Charles, trailing in polls and money, argued he can still win by focusing on affordability. Independent Rick Bennett remained a distant third but positioned himself as a spoiler, agreeing along with Pingree to a fall debate schedule that Charles has resisted.

races.summary: The first polling after Abdul El-Sayed's Aug. 4 primary win over Haley Stevens dominated coverage, with a Fox News poll (Aug. 6-10) showing Republican Mike Rogers ahead 51-47 in the open-seat race. Reporting highlighted El-Sayed's soft favorability (41% favorable, 54% unfavorable) and underperformance with Black voters, women and suburbanites, versus Rogers holding his base and edging independents. The Senate Leadership Fund added $6 million to its Michigan spending (about $51 million total) to run ads branding El-Sayed 'dangerously radical' in the Detroit, Grand Rapids and Flint markets. Rogers rolled out an economy-focused ad, and outside money continued to flood what has become a record-spending cycle in the state.

races.summary: With both nominees set after the Aug. 4 primaries, the race to replace term-limited Gov. Gretchen Whitmer moved into a general-election phase focused on running-mate selection. Republican John James, endorsed by President Trump, named state Rep. Jay DeBoyer as his lieutenant-governor pick on Aug. 13-14, completing the GOP ticket ahead of the party convention. Democrat Jocelyn Benson, the secretary of state, had not yet announced a running mate, weighing legislators including Sarah Anthony, Winnie Brinks and Jim Ananich before an Aug. 25 deadline. National handicappers such as Cook Political Report rate the open swing-state contest as leaning slightly toward Benson, with both candidates agreeing in principle to multiple fall debates.

races.matchup: Jon Husted (R, appointed inc.) vs. Sherrod Brown (D)
races.summary: Coverage was shaped by a Fox News poll (released Aug. 13) showing Democrat Sherrod Brown leading appointed GOP Sen. Jon Husted 53-45, unchanged from June, with inflation and cost of living named the top issue by 40% of voters. Reporting noted 51% of voters worry Husted is 'too close' to Trump, while Brown holds 97% of Democrats to Husted's 87% of Republicans. Brown continued to out-raise Husted and leaned into an anti-data-center message, attacking Husted's record of backing tax breaks for developers. Sabato's Crystal Ball has the race a toss-up, and outside groups including the Senate Leadership Fund are ramping up spending.

races.summary: Coverage over the past two weeks centered on new statewide polling showing the open-seat race essentially tied. A Fox News poll (conducted Aug 6-10) had Ramaswamy up 50-48, while an Emerson College survey showed Acton narrowly ahead 46-45, driving a wave of 'Democrat gains'/'Acton overtakes' stories. Reporting also noted Acton outraising Ramaswamy in the latest fundraising period. The tone modestly favored Acton on momentum, though Ramaswamy retained a slight edge in the higher-turnout Fox model.

races.summary: Two weeks of polling showed Democrat Roy Cooper with a durable lead over Republican Michael Whatley for the open seat vacated by Thom Tillis. The Carolina Journal Poll (Aug. 9-10) put Cooper up 51.5-39, his first time topping 50%, while an Elon University poll released Aug. 12 had him ahead 53-42, and a Fox News survey showed +9. Cooper leads independents by roughly 20 points and holds a wide favorability and name-recognition edge over Whatley, a former RNC and state party chair who has never held elected office. Pollsters cautioned the margin could tighten after Labor Day as ad spending increases and Whatley's recognition grows, but Republicans start the fall well behind.

races.matchup: Jon Ossoff (D, inc.) vs. Mike Collins (R)
races.summary: Coverage split between Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff's structural advantages and mounting controversies around GOP nominee Mike Collins. Ossoff continues to lead in polling (single digits to low double digits) and holds a massive fundraising edge, having raised roughly $81 million cycle-to-date with about $42 million on hand versus Collins' $2 million. Reporting focused on Collins telling a pardoned Jan. 6 defendant in Savannah that wronged Americans deserve compensation, which Ossoff seized on as 'disgraceful,' and on four dozen Black Georgia lawmakers pressing Collins over his son-in-law's alleged white-nationalist posts. Ossoff also faced some negative coverage over criticism from Jewish voters and donors upset with his mixed record on Israel aid. Sabato rates the race Likely D and Cook rates it Lean D.

races.matchup: Rick Jackson (R) vs. Keisha Lance Bottoms (D)
races.summary: The open-seat race stayed a statistical tie, with a late-July/early-August poll showing Bottoms 46.4% to Jackson 44.9%, inside the margin of error. Coverage emphasized Jackson's financial firepower: the healthcare executive has self-funded roughly $50M plus a large ad buy and out-raised Bottoms in the latest reporting period. Jackson also launched a major ad campaign attacking Bottoms in early August, while both candidates campaigned in Athens and across the state. The tone was balanced-Bottoms narrowly ahead on the horse race, Jackson dominant on money and paid media.

races.summary: Coverage over the last two weeks centered on a new Emerson College poll (fielded Aug. 2-4) showing Republican Ashley Hinson narrowly ahead of Democrat Josh Turek, 48% to 45%, within the 3.7-point margin of error. Reporting framed the open-seat race to replace retiring Sen. Joni Ernst as one of the closest Senate contests of 2026, noting Turek's lower unfavorables and a recent Obama endorsement against Hinson's Trump backing and higher name recognition. Iowa Republicans launched a statewide 'Turek's Too Liberal Tour' the same day the poll dropped. Overall tone was competitive and balanced, tilting slightly Republican given Hinson's fresh polling lead.

races.summary: Coverage framed Auditor Rob Sand as the front-runner in the open race to replace retiring Gov. Kim Reynolds, citing an Emerson/Nexstar poll showing Sand 48% to Lahn 43% and Sand's record-breaking fundraising haul. GOP nominee Zach Lahn-an anti-establishment businessman who upset Trump-backed Rep. Randy Feenstra in the primary-pushed a populist 'truth is on the ballot' message at the Iowa State Fair. Lahn spent much of the period on defense, criticizing Democratic attacks on his residency and family. The tone tilted toward Sand on both polling and money.

races.matchup: Joe Lombardo (R, inc.) vs. Aaron Ford (D)
races.summary: Coverage described a tight, high-spending contest between GOP incumbent Joe Lombardo and Democratic AG Aaron Ford, with polls diverging-one mid-July DGA survey had them tied at 44%, while a late-July GOP poll gave Lombardo a seven-point edge. Lombardo has vastly outspent Ford (reported at roughly 168-to-1 since December) and gone up early with ads, including Spanish-language spots. Ford, a fluent Spanish speaker, focused on affordability, housing and cost-of-living while courting Latino voters. The tone was roughly neutral, with Lombardo's incumbency and spending advantage offset by Ford's competitiveness in polling.

races.summary: Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley won the Aug. 11 Democratic primary in a photo finish, edging democratic socialist state Rep. Francesca Hong by about half a point (roughly 39.8%-39.4%), setting up a general election against Trump-backed Rep. Tom Tiffany. On Aug. 13, Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the open-seat race from Toss-up to Leans Democratic, calling Crowley a modest favorite. Within days both campaigns launched dueling seven-figure ad blitzes, with Tiffany's spots branding Crowley a 'failed executive' of Milwaukee County and both sides targeting western Wisconsin. The cycle was strongly D-favorable given the primary result and the ratings shift, though Tiffany moved aggressively to define Crowley.

races.matchup: Katie Hobbs (D, inc.) vs. Andy Biggs (R)
races.summary: The general election between Gov. Katie Hobbs and GOP Rep. Andy Biggs opened sharply negative, with Hobbs releasing an attack ad tying Biggs to Trump's agenda within minutes of his July 21 primary win. An AARP-commissioned poll released Aug. 6 showed Hobbs leading Biggs 52% to 44% among likely voters. Her advantage is driven by voters under 50, while Biggs leads among older voters and those without college degrees. Coverage over the two weeks centered on Hobbs's polling edge and the increasingly combative tone of the race.

races.matchup: Chris Pappas (D) vs. John E. Sununu (R)
races.summary: In-window coverage was lighter than other states because both primaries are still ahead on Sept. 8, but WBUR's mid-August feature framed New Hampshire as a pivotal Senate battleground notable for candidates avoiding their parties' ideological extremes. Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas, favored to win his primary, is running as a middle-class champion and holds a modest polling edge, while former Sen. John E. Sununu leads Scott Brown for the GOP nod and is backed by national Republican super PACs and a Trump endorsement. Analysts quoted expect a razor-thin general election. The tone leaned mildly Democratic, reflecting Pappas's slight advantage in the open race to succeed retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen.

articles.headline: New Hampshire has a key U.S. Senate race - without the extremes of other states

races.matchup: Kelly Ayotte (R, inc.) vs. Cinde Warmington (D)
races.summary: The confirmed Democratic challenger to incumbent Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte is former Executive Councilor Cinde Warmington, who is making her second gubernatorial bid ahead of the Sept. 8 primary. In-window coverage was largely unfavorable to the Democrat: on Aug. 11, Warmington released a video defending her past lobbying work for OxyContin maker Purdue Pharma, responding to a sustained Ayotte attack campaign of ads, billboards and signs tying her to the opioid crisis. Earlier reporting showed Ayotte holding a mid-single-digit polling lead and a roughly six-to-one fundraising advantage with about $2 million on hand. Warmington remained relatively unknown to many voters, framing the race around affordability, housing and taxes.

races.summary: In the Aug. 4 primaries to succeed term-limited Gov. Laura Kelly, Kansas Senate President Ty Masterson won a crowded, expensive seven-way GOP field on the strength of a Trump endorsement, taking about 43% over rivals including Phil Sarnecki, Vicki Schmidt and Scott Schwab. Democrat Cindy Holscher won her party's nomination with roughly 49%, overcoming Gov. Kelly's endorsement of a rival and defeating Overland Park Mayor Curt Skoog. The matchup sets a Masterson-Holscher general election in a Republican-leaning state. Coverage was largely neutral results reporting focused on the primary outcomes and Trump's role in the GOP contest.

races.matchup: Kurt Alme (R) vs. Alani Bankhead (D) vs. Seth Bodnar (I)
races.summary: Coverage over the past two weeks centered almost entirely on Democratic disarray in Montana's open-seat race. As the Aug. 10 withdrawal deadline passed, both Democratic nominee Alani Bankhead and independent Seth Bodnar refused to drop out, keeping the anti-GOP vote split and, analysts noted, easing Republican Kurt Alme's path to victory. Twenty-two Democratic state legislators and former Sens. Jon Tester and Max Baucus publicly urged Bankhead to exit and back Bodnar, who polls competitively against Alme head-to-head. Bankhead insisted she is 'in this race to win it,' while Bodnar vowed to stay 'until the very end.' The framing was largely one of a fractured Democratic-aligned field boosting the GOP nominee.

races.matchup: Dan Sullivan (R, inc.) vs. Mary Peltola (D)
races.summary: With the Aug. 18 top-four primary approaching, coverage focused on Democrat Mary Peltola's fundraising dominance and narrow polling edge over Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan, with an early-August survey showing her about two points ahead. A dominant storyline was millions in outside super PAC money suddenly flowing to fringe, low-profile candidates in an apparent bid to game Alaska's ranked-choice system and weaken both frontrunners before November. Reporting also tracked the ongoing 'two Dan Sullivans' saga, in which a same-named Republican challenger from Petersburg remains under FBI and state investigation over whether the candidacy was engineered to confuse voters. Both Sullivan and Peltola are expected to easily advance, leaving the remaining two general-election slots uncertain. The tone modestly favored Peltola given her cash advantage and polling position.

races.matchup: Pete Ricketts (R, inc.) vs. Dan Osborn (I)
races.summary: Coverage in the first half of August emphasized how competitive the race remains, with public polling continuing to show independent Dan Osborn statistically tied with Republican incumbent Pete Ricketts. The two campaigns agreed to a Sept. 1 debate at the BigIron Events Center during the Nebraska State Fair, moderated by News Channel Nebraska with a panel of state outlets. On the trail, Ricketts brought his campaign to Kearney on Aug. 11, repeatedly branding his opponent 'Democrat Dan' and calling him out of step with Nebraskans, while Osborn continued a populist tour aimed at all 93 counties. The framing largely cast Osborn as a viable underdog against a better-funded incumbent, keeping the overall tone near neutral.

races.summary: The past two weeks were dominated by favorable news for Democrat James Talarico, who led or ran even with Republican Ken Paxton across multiple polls, including a Texas Southern University survey marking the third straight poll with Talarico ahead. Fundraising coverage was especially lopsided: Talarico has raised roughly $72 million to Paxton's $16.8 million and ended June with more than triple the cash on hand, drawing heavily on small-dollar donors. Reporting depicted Paxton pleading for donations, appealing to the Washington establishment he once attacked, and trying to tamp down growing Republican anxiety about his campaign after a bruising primary win over incumbent John Cornyn. Cook Political Report still rates the seat 'Lean Republican,' but the coverage tilted clearly toward Talarico's momentum.

races.matchup: Greg Abbott (R, inc.) vs. Gina Hinojosa (D)
races.summary: The race between Gov. Greg Abbott, seeking a record fourth term, and Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa tightened sharply in early August, with multiple polls showing a statistical tie. A Texas A&M Bush School/ReconMR survey put Abbott at 46% and Hinojosa at 45%, echoing a Fox News poll showing a one-point race, a roughly five-point swing toward Hinojosa since June as her name recognition and favorability rose. At an Aug. 6 Houston rally marking the Voting Rights Act anniversary, Hinojosa called the contest the 'most important' race in America. Coverage increasingly framed the race as newly competitive and driven by Hinojosa's momentum.

Alex Vindman, the well-funded Trump-impeachment witness (roughly $14.5M raised through June), and progressive state Rep. Angie Nixon, framed repeatedly as a test of establishment versus progressive direction for Florida Democrats. Appointed GOP Sen. Amy Klobuchar won the DFL nomination with roughly 90% of the vote, becoming the first woman to lead a major-party ticket for Minnesota governor after Gov. Tim Walz withdrew. State House Speaker Lisa Demuth won the GOP nomination with about 43%, defeating a field that included Mike Lindell, and also became the first woman to win her party's nod. The result sets up a historic all-women general election, guaranteeing Minnesota will elect its first female governor on Nov. 3. Coverage emphasized Klobuchar's dominant margin and the historic nature of the matchup.
